summary: No-ship: the proposed shared interfaces cannot preserve existing authorization, planner-state, and scan-totality contracts. Implementing them literally risks wrong auto-merge decisions or false-green guards.

facts.relaunchTail: This is a property of the run, not of the repository, so the round's next launch may use another backend (--reviewer claude) — the caller performs that switch as its second launch; this launcher never spawns a second backend itself.

triage: review-gate SKILL.md §§ Triage and Rounds govern. Render EVERY finding as a full table row — `ID | Finding (title + full body) | Severity | file:line | Code | Recommendation | Proposed decision` — never truncated and never inside a dialog; then ask the ROUND before the rows — take every Proposed decision as it stands, or decide row by row — and `as proposed` ends the round in that ONE action; only if row-by-row was chosen, ask per finding with that row's Proposed decision as the first option, a reject or defer taking a free-text reason; echo back ONLY the rows that carried free text, and none if the round was decided by selection alone. Max 2 rounds. Append the decided rows to `docs/reviews/<slug>/decisions.md` under a `### <gate> r<n> (<reviewer>)` heading — one line per row, `<ID> <decision> — <finding title>[; <reason for reject/defer>]`, and an accepted waiver as `WAIVED by user: <reason>` — then COMMIT it with this artifact. That grammar is not decoration: the conductors anchor on `^### <gate> r<n>` and read the waiver line as the pass condition, so a ledger written in any other shape reads back as a gate still owed.

findings.title: Plan.action cannot represent valid non-actionable outcomes
findings.body: The planner currently emits four semantically distinct actions: `noop`, `refuse`, `bump`, and `propose-pr`. Restricting `action` to the two-value authorization lane makes valid refusal/no-op results unrepresentable. Implementations must either discard those outcomes, misclassify them as mutation lanes, or contradict the design. Because the plan crosses a JSON boundary, the TypeScript union alone also cannot prevent malformed values from being silently filtered by the consumer.
findings.code:
**이동 콜사이트**: poll-ghcr.ts · run-bump-plan.ts · ensure-bump-pr.ts · bump-tag.ts.
`action` 필드는 `Lane` union으로 — 오타가 런타임 skip이 아니라 컴파일 red.
findings.recommendation: Define a runtime-decoded discriminated union such as `Change { lane, candidate, ... } | Noop | Refusal`; place `Lane` only on actionable changes and reject malformed serialized plans.

findings.title: The target identity is ambiguous across app and platform namespaces
findings.body: `resolveLane(root, app)` and `branchFor(app, tag)` omit whether the target is an app surface or a bespoke platform component. The repository already has `platform/files` as a bump target, while create-app does not reserve platform names, so `apps/files` is permitted. Same-name targets can then share a branch while resolving authorization from different files (`.bindings.json` versus `.image-pin.json`). This can overwrite one target's PR or apply the other target's autoDeploy policy, including arming a PR that requires human approval.
findings.code:
**interface**: `Plan` 타입(항목 optionality 포함) + `Lane` union(`"bump" | "propose-pr"`) +
`branchFor(app, tag)` + `commitMessage(app, tag)` + `WRITER_IDENT` +
`resolveLane(root, app)`(현행 `planApp`/`probeLane`의 **유일 구현**).
findings.recommendation: Introduce a discriminated target identity such as `{kind: "app" | "component", name}` into plan items, lane resolution, and branch naming. Alternatively, enforce and test global name disjointness before creation and fail closed if both policy sources exist.

findings.title: guardMain cannot preserve multi-domain and machine-output contracts
findings.body: The singular `{label, min, enumerate}` model cannot represent the listed guards. `check-alert-rules` has four independently meaningful SCAN domains/floors, while `check-guard-authority` has two domains and a `--json` mode where stdout must contain JSON only. Leaving additional floors or markers inside `check` reintroduces the exact ordering drift the kernel claims to eliminate; emitting the marker unconditionally corrupts machine-readable output. The kernel therefore cannot own the promised sequence for all migrated callers as designed.
findings.code:
- `tools/lib/scan-floor.ts`: `guardMain({label, min, enumerate, check})`.
  seam 뒤로 들어가는 것: **열거 → 바닥값 판정 → SCAN 방출 → 검사 → 종료코드** 순서
  전체. 셸 커널 `scripts/lib/scan-floor.sh`(소비자 15, 콜사이트↔방출 대조 테스트 보유)의
  TS 이식이다.
findings.recommendation: Model a collection of named scan domains with independent floors, plus an explicit output/emission policy. Require every floor to pass before emitting any SCAN marker, then run the domain check once.

findings.title: readLedger lacks the observed domain required for bilateral reconciliation
findings.body: `path`, `container`, and `entrySchema` are sufficient to load and validate stored JSON, but not to detect undeclared observations or dead declarations. Existing consumers use materially different reconciliation semantics: nested workflow/job identities, CI-step coverage rules, and image artifact wildcard/exemption matching. Implementing bilateral reconciliation behind this signature either omits required inputs or forces domain policy into hidden coupling and risks false-green ledgers.
findings.code:
- `tools/lib/policy-ledger.ts`: `readLedger({path, container, entrySchema})`.
  seam 뒤로: 컨테이너 shape(현행 4가지 → 1가지, 주석 키 `_readme`/`$comment` 통일),
  `schema-check.ts` 재사용 항목 검증, **미선언·죽은-선언 양방향 대조**(현행 3벌 복제),
  fail-closed 로딩(빈 원장 = red).
findings.recommendation: Either narrow `readLedger` to fail-closed loading and schema validation, or define a separate reconciliation interface that explicitly accepts observed identities, key/matcher semantics, and justified exemptions.

Add design-level cases for noop/refuse plans, malformed serialized plans, same-name app/component targets, multi-domain scans, and JSON-only guard output.
